bull_bear.body:
- ~INR600 cr invested to acquire the two O&M portfolios (debt-funded; the ~INR40 cr "other income" is the return on that).
- Future FCF: first integrate acquisitions, then opportunistic acquisitions (≤10–20% of FCF), with dividend/buyback "in interest of shareholders" to be decided by Board post-consolidation.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Earnings quality:** large slice of EBITDA/other income is acquisition/debt-related and not-yet-consolidated operating profit — headline ~50% margin drops to ~45% ex that.
- **Timing risk:** FY27 INR600 cr depends on NCLT/EOI approvals landing for both acquired entities (final phases; 60–90 days).
- **Group execution credibility:** investors flagged repeated guidance misses at Inox Wind (MW→revenue guidance switch; INR5,000 cr → INR4,600 cr FY26 on ECS supply-chain/geopolitical delays, PSU payment delays).
- **Related-party concentration:** Inox Clean is the dominant future order source for the group — cycle/governance dependency.
- **Solar BESS substitution / FDRE battery focus** raised as a structural question for wind demand.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Confident, defensive under pointed minority-shareholder pushback on value destruction and guidance misses; Devansh Jain emphasizes 4-yr value creation, "only Indian wind player that survived with zero haircut," renewable arm "valued north of $10bn." Combative ("don't hold us responsible for a world war"). FY27 75% growth framed as "conservative."
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- Sector consolidation thesis: of 5 wind players, "2 allied, 3 bankrupt; we acquired 2 of the 3 bankrupt" — Inox Green is structurally cornering Indian wind O&M.
- INR700 cr accumulated-loss tax shield → near-100% cash conversion of FY27 EBITDA.
- Evacuation-infra demerger is the real ROE/ROCE lever (gross block + depreciation stripped out), not just operating growth.
- Inox Wind's pivot to 75–80% equipment supply (from 100% turnkey 24 months ago) indirectly de-risks Green's parent and working capital.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- 'An Asset-light Growth-oriented Annuity Business Model' — 'Asset-light balance sheet post the demerger; Focus: Long-term contracts with steady cashflows'.
- Capital is being deployed inorganically: the portfolio figure includes 'the investments made to acquire ~ 6.5 GW of operational wind O&M portfolio of two companies', and management calls the Wind World transaction 'value accretive for shareholders'.
- The deck offers a forward earnings framing rather than a payout policy: 'Post completion of the acquisitions and consolidation of financials, Inox Green's consolidated EBITDA and PAT are expected to increase multifold.'
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Described as a 'Subsidiary of IWL; India's leading renewable O&M services player with ~13.3 GWp of assets under management. Inox Green is India's only listed pure-play renewable O&M service company.'
- The moat claimed is group inter-play: Inox Wind (one of India's largest wind turbine manufacturing players) has a 'Robust orderbook of ~4.4 GW as on July'26', and group IPP platform Inox Clean targets 3 GW+ annual capacity addition of which '~20% - 30% ... is expected to be wind', giving Inox Green 'multi-year multi-GW portfolio growth'.
- Sponsor backing is framed as 'Strong support from sponsor, INOXGFL Group, a USD 16 bn Indian conglomerate with deep interests across chemicals and renewables' (group size stated as on June 30, 2026 at INR:USD Rs. 96).
- Established track record of more than 14 years in wind energy O&M, with 'Robust relationships with renewable asset owners – customers include PSUs, IPPs and private investors'.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] The Wind World India (erstwhile Enercon India) ~4.5 GW wind O&M portfolio 'generated revenue of Rs. 580 crore in FY26 and benefits from contracted annual price escalation of approximately 5%'; its client base includes the Tata Group, ReNew, Greenko Group, Apraava Energy and Hindustan Zinc, with assets across Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh.
- [Demerger] 'Demerger of the power evacuation business has been completed as on August 1 2026 (being the record date)'; the deck also flags '# Restatement of financials due to discontinued operations' against the Q1 FY26 comparatives.
- [Group structure] INOXGFL Group has a legacy of over nine decades with three listed entities, spanning fluoropolymers and fluorochemicals (Gujarat Fluorochemicals, largest PTFE/fluoropolymer manufacturer in India), battery chemicals, wind turbines (Inox Wind: 2MW, 3MW and upcoming 4MW class WTGs), EPC (IRSL, formerly Resco Global), renewable O&M (IGESL), and solar cells & modules; Inox Solar targets 11 GW of solar cell & module manufacturing capacity across India and the USA and Inox Neo targets 14 GW of hybrid RE capacity by FY29.
- [Sector backdrop] The deck cites India's RE capacity (ex-large hydro) at ~237 GW as of Jun'26 with 13.9 GW added in Q1 FY27; of 9.34 GW awarded through tenders in Q1 FY27, 4.55 GW (49%) was wind/Hybrid/FDRE; India targets 500 GW/1,800 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030/2047; onshore wind potential is put at 695 GW at 120m hub height and 1,164 GW at 150m hub height, with 8-10 GW annual wind installations expected in the near term.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] The Wind World India (erstwhile Enercon India) ~4.5 GW wind O&M portfolio 'generated revenue of Rs. 580 crore in FY26 and benefits from contracted annual price escalation of approximately 5%'; its client base includes the Tata Group, ReNew, Greenko Group, Apraava Energy and Hindustan Zinc, with assets across Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh.
- [Demerger] 'Demerger of the power evacuation business has been completed as on August 1 2026 (being the record date)'; the deck also flags '# Restatement of financials due to discontinued operations' against the Q1 FY26 comparatives.
- [Group structure] INOXGFL Group has a legacy of over nine decades with three listed entities, spanning fluoropolymers and fluorochemicals (Gujarat Fluorochemicals, largest PTFE/fluoropolymer manufacturer in India), battery chemicals, wind turbines (Inox Wind: 2MW, 3MW and upcoming 4MW class WTGs), EPC (IRSL, formerly Resco Global), renewable O&M (IGESL), and solar cells & modules; Inox Solar targets 11 GW of solar cell & module manufacturing capacity across India and the USA and Inox Neo targets 14 GW of hybrid RE capacity by FY29.
- [Sector backdrop] The deck cites India's RE capacity (ex-large hydro) at ~237 GW as of Jun'26 with 13.9 GW added in Q1 FY27; of 9.34 GW awarded through tenders in Q1 FY27, 4.55 GW (49%) was wind/Hybrid/FDRE; India targets 500 GW/1,800 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030/2047; onshore wind potential is put at 695 GW at 120m hub height and 1,164 GW at 150m hub height, with 8-10 GW annual wind installations expected in the near term.

one-line thesis: Inox Green is consolidating into India's largest renewable O&M player via two large inorganic wind-OEM portfolio buys (4.5 GW + 2 GW) on top of organic growth, targeting FY27 EBITDA >INR600 cr (50%-ish margin, near-full cash conversion, INR700 cr tax shield) — but a chunk of current reported profit is acquisition-related "other income" not yet consolidated, so headline quality is soft until the deals formally fold in.
financial scorecard (inox green standalo:
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | YoY | Notes / one-offs |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total income | INR120 cr | +40% | Core O&M op-revenue ~INR69 cr (vs INR78 cr Q3 — QoQ dip from value-add timing) |
| EBITDA | INR57 cr | +93% | Margin elevated by ~INR40 cr acquisition-related other income |
| PBT | INR46 cr | +244% | — |
| PAT | INR28 cr | +340% | — |
| Cash PAT | INR46 cr | +327% | — |
| Other income (consol) | INR60.8 cr | — | ~INR40 cr from 2 strategic acquisitions (debt-related), ~INR10 cr value-add services, ~INR10 cr treasury |
| FY26 turnover | INR426 cr | — | FY26 EBITDA ~INR210 cr (~50% margin; ~45% ex acquisition income) |
| FY26 cash back | INR158 cr | — | — |
| Portfolio | 13+ GWp | — | ~10.5 GW wind + balance solar; machine availability ~96.5% |
| Gross block removed | ~INR1,000 cr | — | Evacuation infra demerged to IRSL; ~INR50–55 cr/yr depreciation eliminated (lifts ROE/ROCE) |
guidance (verify next quarter):
- **FY27 EBITDA upwards of INR600 cr** (reaffirmed), driven by full consolidation of the two acquired portfolios + organic adds. Mgmt says ~all of the INR600 cr converts to operating cash profit (no depreciation post-demerger, no finance cost, INR700 cr loss tax-shield).
- O&M to rise from ~10% to ~18–20% of group (Inox Wind + Green) revenue mix as acquisitions consolidate.
- **Watch-item:** FY27 EBITDA hinges on accruals from acquired entities effective 1-Apr-26 even if legal merger slips to Q1/Q2 — confirm consolidation actually lands in Q1 FY27 results.
order book & pipeline:
- O&M portfolio 13+ GWp; pipeline fed by group Inox Clean's 3 GW+/yr additions (14 GW by FY29) and Inox Wind external execution (3.1 GW order book).
- Inorganic: two bankrupt wind-OEM O&M portfolios (4.5 GW + ~2 GW) acquired; first NCLT order expected "next couple of weeks," second in 60–90 days. ~50% EBITDA margin on acquired books (OEM substations/evacuation systems).
- A "couple of GW" further acquisition targets lined up (≤10–20% of FCF).
segment / subsidiary detail:
- **Core O&M:** ~96.5% machine availability; WTG overhaul / life-extension packages launched (high-growth optionality).
- **Evacuation infra:** demerged out into Inox Renewable Solutions (NCLT Ahmedabad approved); IRSL to auto-list post approvals. Removes ~INR1,000 cr gross block and ~INR50–55 cr/yr depreciation from Inox Green.
- **Digital:** exploring "Agent AI" on low value-add roles; Vayuveer/Inox Learning Academy producing ~600 skilled techs/yr (hiring Agniveers).
growth verticals / optionality:
- Largest renewable O&M co in India near-term; "one of largest globally by 2030."
- WTG life-extension/overhaul as a new high-margin service line.
- Group "ONE INTEGRATED" flywheel: Inox Clean capacity adds → recurring O&M for Green; Inox Wind equipment supply.
- Potential dividend/buyback once two acquisitions consolidate (no policy yet).
margins & cost dynamics:
- O&M is a ~50% EBITDA-margin business; FY26 ~50% reported, ~45% ex acquisition-related income (per CFO).
- Acquisitions add ~50% margin OEM portfolios. Post-demerger depreciation removal materially lifts ROE/ROCE.
- Quarterly margin lumpy due to value-add service timing — should be judged annualized.
capex / expansion:
- Inox Green growth is largely inorganic (portfolio acquisitions) + organic O&M onboarding, capital-light vs manufacturing siblings.
- Group capex heavy at Inox Clean (10 GW IPP / 10 GW cell / 10 GW module "10^3" over 15 months) and Inox Wind (power electronics, transformers, cranes in-house) — indirect Green demand driver.
capital allocation:
- ~INR600 cr invested to acquire the two O&M portfolios (debt-funded; the ~INR40 cr "other income" is the return on that).
- Future FCF: first integrate acquisitions, then opportunistic acquisitions (≤10–20% of FCF), with dividend/buyback "in interest of shareholders" to be decided by Board post-consolidation.
risks & watch-items:
- **Earnings quality:** large slice of EBITDA/other income is acquisition/debt-related and not-yet-consolidated operating profit — headline ~50% margin drops to ~45% ex that.
- **Timing risk:** FY27 INR600 cr depends on NCLT/EOI approvals landing for both acquired entities (final phases; 60–90 days).
- **Group execution credibility:** investors flagged repeated guidance misses at Inox Wind (MW→revenue guidance switch; INR5,000 cr → INR4,600 cr FY26 on ECS supply-chain/geopolitical delays, PSU payment delays).
- **Related-party concentration:** Inox Clean is the dominant future order source for the group — cycle/governance dependency.
- **Solar BESS substitution / FDRE battery focus** raised as a structural question for wind demand.
management quality / tone: - Confident, defensive under pointed minority-shareholder pushback on value destruction and guidance misses; Devansh Jain emphasizes 4-yr value creation, "only Indian wind player that survived with zero haircut," renewable arm "valued north of $10bn." Combative ("don't hold us responsible for a world war"). FY27 75% growth framed as "conservative."
non-obvious takeaways:
- Sector consolidation thesis: of 5 wind players, "2 allied, 3 bankrupt; we acquired 2 of the 3 bankrupt" — Inox Green is structurally cornering Indian wind O&M.
- INR700 cr accumulated-loss tax shield → near-100% cash conversion of FY27 EBITDA.
- Evacuation-infra demerger is the real ROE/ROCE lever (gross block + depreciation stripped out), not just operating growth.
- Inox Wind's pivot to 75–80% equipment supply (from 100% turnkey 24 months ago) indirectly de-risks Green's parent and working capital.

| Earnings quality / acquisition-income dependence | — | INOXGREEN · 543667 (self) | ~INR40 cr of EBITDA is acquisition/debt income; margin ~45% ex it. Med risk until consolidation |
| FDRE battery / solar+BESS substitution of wind | GFCL EV (code unverified, group BESS) | Pure wind-equipment demand | FDRE projects shifting to battery firming pressures standalone wind. Low-Med |

themes.title: Renewable IPP / FDRE firm-power & storage
themes.need: DISCOMs mandating firm/round-the-clock RE make BESS + pumped-hydro the bid differentiator, and in Q1FY27 storage demand ran ahead of supply. ADANIGREEN has 3.5 GWh of BESS installed (+1.9 GWh at Khavda this quarter), targets 10+ GWh this fiscal and 50 GWh by FY30 on a thumb-rule INR 25-30 lakh of EBITDA per MWh against ~INR 1.5cr/MWh of capex, and has contracted essentially all merchant/C&I capacity to sibling AESL on 25-year (solar/wind) and 15-year (battery) fixed-price PPAs targeting ~15-16% IRR - a pivot from merchant builder to fixed-return contracted IPP, with evacuation (not panels) named as the binding constraint. JSWENERGY added 873 MW in Q1 and ~1.1 GW since April - 36% of its 3 GW FY27 target already banked, Tidong Hydro commissioned four months early - and raised INR 10,150cr, taking net leverage 5.2x to 4.95x. On the equipment side SERVOTECH said its BESS pack capacity is fully booked ('we are not able to meet the demand') and committed to 2x capacity in 6 months, 3x by 21-Mar-2027 and 10x within 2 years. ACMESOLAR/KPIGREEN/SUZLON/INOXWIND attach storage to solar/wind; NTPC/NHPC/SJVN/TATAPOWER drive pumped-hydro and utility-scale storage.
themes.driver: BESS capacity commissioning against demand two independent managements (ADANIGREEN, SERVOTECH) say already exceeds supply; FDRE/peak-power tender awards; merchant DAM prices (JSWENERGY: INR 4.40 -> INR 5.10/unit, +16%) on +8.5% Q1 power demand.
